marks.gloss_en: meat of desire was permitted in the Land because they were far from the Tabernacle; all the more so now in exile, when they are farther
Rav Yosef: all the more so now [in exile], when they are farther still -- meat of desire is permitted
now that even non-kosher food (cuts of pig) was permitted them in the seven years of conquest, is stabbed meat [of a kosher animal] a question?
דכתיב ובתים מלאים כל טוב
ואמר רבי ירמיה בר אבא אמר רב: כתלי דחזירי -- the 'good things' were cuts of pig meat
in the seven years of conquest, even non-kosher food was permitted to them
דתניא: R' Akiva -- meat of stabbing, permitted at first, was forbidden in the Land
Rav Yosef: rather, the tanna of 'one may always slaughter' is R' Akiva
בשלמא לרבי ישמעאל, היינו דכתיב ושחט את בן הבקר
אלא לרבי עקיבא מאי ושחט? -- if stabbing was permitted in the wilderness, why is slaughter written for the offering?
קדשים שאני -- sacrificial animals are different
'and he shall slaughter the young bull' (Lev 1:5)
בשלמא לרבי ישמעאל, היינו דכתיב הצאן ובקר ישחט להם
אלא לרבי עקיבא מאי הצאן ובקר ישחט להם? ינחר להם מיבעי ליה -- the wilderness verse should have said 'stabbed'
נחירה שלהן זו היא שחיטתן -- their stabbing is their slaughter
'shall flocks and herds be slaughtered for them' (Num 11:22)
בשלמא לרבי ישמעאל, היינו דתנן: ... והנוחר והמעקר פטור מלכסות
אלא לרבי עקיבא אמאי פטור מלכסות? -- if stabbing was once a permitted way of killing, why is one who stabs exempt from covering the blood?
the mishna (85a): one who slaughters and it became a carcass in his hand, and one who stabs or rips, is exempt from covering [the blood]
בשלמא לרבי עקיבא דאמר בשר תאוה לא איתסר כלל, היינו דכתיב אך כאשר יאכל את הצבי ואת האיל
אלא לרבי ישמעאל, צבי ואיל גופיה מי הוי שרי? -- if meat of desire was forbidden in the wilderness, were gazelle and deer themselves permitted?
'only as the gazelle and the deer are eaten, so shall you eat it' (Deut 12:22)
הואיל ואיתסר, איתסר -- since it was forbidden, it was forbidden
כי אסר רחמנא -- בהמה דחזיא להקרבה, אבל חיה דלא חזיא להקרבה לא אסר רחמנא -- the prohibition was of a domestic animal fit for offering, not of a wild animal unfit for it
שנית הכל שוחטין ולעולם שוחטין, בכל שוחטים מאי משנית ליה? וכי תימא בין בצור... הא דומיא דהנך קתני -- the clauses must be read alike, and 'with anything' cannot be read of the slaughtered
the same question against the reading of 'one may always slaughter' as concerning the slaughtered (meat of stabbing): 'with anything' cannot be read in parallel
the mishna (15b): one may slaughter with anything
Rav Yosef: now that they are exiled, one might think they revert to the first permission -- therefore the mishna says 'one must always slaughter'
R' Akiva holds: meat of desire was never forbidden at all
R' Yirmeya: limbs of stabbed meat that Israel brought with them into the Land -- what is their law?
rather, R' Yirmeya's question concerns the period after [the seven years]
Rabba: 'with anything' is taught like the other two clauses -- if they concern those who slaughter, so does it; if those slaughtered, so does it
Rava: 'all slaughter' -- one [such clause] includes a Kuti, and one includes an apostate Jew
כמגירה שנינו -- the reply rests on the mishna's exclusion of the saw
the mishna: [one may slaughter with anything] except the harvest sickle
